title: Immediate implant placement and immediate loading with all-ceramic crowns in the premolar region. A prospective controlled clinical study
summary:
Background:
If a tooth in the esthetically visible area can no longer be preserved and needs to be removed, it is ideally important to plan in advance how the resulting gap will be restored. This is particularly important to maintain both chewing function and aesthetics.
One treatment option is the use of a dental implant. Typically, the implant is loaded with a single crown after a healing period of about three months.
However, the concept of immediate implant placement with immediate loading has become increasingly important. In this approach, the implant is placed immediately after tooth extraction, following the restoration with a single crown. So far, there are only a few scientific studies that have evaluated the effectiveness and safety of this treatment approach in the esthetically visible area, using an implant-supported single crown made of all-ceramic material.
Function and of course aesthetics are especially important in the esthetically visible area. The planned study will therefore investigate how the immediate implant placement with immediate loading will perform in the esthetically visible area in the long term, and how satisfied patients will be with this kind of treatment approach. In addition, the study aims to provide important insights into the conditions under which an immediately loaded implant supported single crown can be considered a reliable treatment option. 
Research Question:
The research question of this study is whether an implant placed immediately after tooth extraction in the esthetically visible area, followed by the immediate restoration with a single crown provides stable long-term outcomes in terms of function, aesthetics, and patient satisfaction, compared to an implant that is loaded after a three-month healing period.
Methods:											          
This study compares two different treatment approaches, each carried out in a separate group. The participants will be randomly assigned to one of the two groups.
In the first group, a single-tooth implant will be placed immediately after tooth extraction and will be restored with an all-ceramic single crown. This means the patients will receive a functional, definitive tooth replacement during the same appointment.
In the second group, a single-tooth implant will also be placed immediately after tooth extraction, however, it will be restored with a definitive all-ceramic crown after a healing period of 3 months.
During the study, several follow-up visits will be conducted to monitor the implant and the implant-supported crown. The follow-up examinations will take place after 6 months, 1 year, 2, 3, 4, and 5 years. During the follow-up examinations, clinical, radiological, functional, and patient-reported parameters will be assessed. This will follow standard procedures used in routine dental care.
In addition, the clinical data collected within the study will be further analysed to systematically investigate the treatment outcomes and any potential complications. The participants will be ask to complete questionnaires to share their personal assessment of various subjective aspects. For this reason, not only objective clinical findings will be considered but also the participant’s experience and satisfaction with the treatment.
conditions: Non-restorable premolar in the upper or lower jaw requiring extraction, implant placement and implant-supported single-tooth restoration

interventions.name:
Arm 1: Treatment Group – Immediate implant placement with immediate loading
Patients will undergo extraction of a non-restorable premolar followed by immediate implant placement. The implant will be loaded within 48 hours with a screw-retained all-ceramic single crown.
Postoperative follow-up exam

Arm 2: Control Group – Immediate implant placement with conventional delayed loading
Patients will undergo extraction of a non-restorable premolar followed by immediate implant placement. Prosthetic rehabilitation with a screw-retained all-ceramic single crown will be performed after a three-month

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients with a non-restorable premolar in the upper or the lower jaw that has to be extracted and replaced with an immediate implant achieving a minimum primary stability of 30 Ncm will be included. Participation additionally requires the patient's consent to take part in the study and to attend the scheduled follow-up appointments. Furthermore, sufficiently good compliance must be present.
Exclusion criteria:
Patients under 18 years of age will be excluded. Also excluded are patients with medical or general health contraindications for the surgical procedure. These include head and neck radiotherapy, current steroid treatment, and antiresorptive therapy. Neurological or psychiatric conditions that impair oral hygiene also constitute an exclusion criterion, as does heavy cigarette consumption of more than 10 cigarettes per day, as well as alcohol and/or drug abuse. Furthermore, patients with uncontrolled or untreated periodontal disease or mucositis will be excluded.
Implant insertion with an implant insertion torque of less than 30 Ncm constitutes an intraoperative exclusion criterion.
